newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan spring crop growth ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan spring crop growth ahead of average.

text.p: Saskatchewan spring crop growth was ahead of the five-year 1992/96 average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.

Thirty two percent of spring cereals were jointed compared to the average 17 percent. Twenty percent of flax tillered compared with the average of 12 percent. Thirty eight percent of canola was at or past the rosette stage compared to the average of 18 percent. Fifteen percent of fall cereals were in the dough stage versus the average of 12 percent.
Most of the crop damage of the past week was caused by flooding, hail, wind and drought conditions.
Rainfall was scattered with some areas remaining dry. The driest region is centred around Weyburn.

An average 11 mm (0.4 inch) of rain fell on the southern grainbelt with up to 50 mm (2 inches) around Whitewood and Rocanville. Drought damage was concentrated in the southeast with some dryness reported in the south central region.

Central Saskatchewan reported an average of 24 mm (0.9 inch) of rain, but Langenburg saw 60 mm (2.4 inches). Hail flattened canola crops in the east-central region and a few pockets reported drought damage. Flea beetles continued to be the most commonly reported insect damage.

Northern districts saw an average 30 mm (1.2 inch) of rain as Ridgedale saw 60 mm (2.4 inches). Drought stress was relieved by rains in the north-central region. The northern flax crop was most advanced in Saskatchewan with 30 percent in the tillering stage while the northern canola crop was furthest behind at 28 percent at or past the rosette stage.
